label: EU7-F16
statement: Pioglitazone | In lists: 5, 6 (B) | Main reason: Age-related risks include bladder cancer, fractures and heart failure. Use for more than one year has been associated with an increased risk of bladder cancer. May increase the incidence of fractures of the upper arms, hands and feet in female diabetics (compared to other oral antidiabetic agents). Can cause fluid retention in older adults, which may exacerbate or precipitate heart failure | Dose adjustment/special considerations: (blank: per ESM note, no suggestion by experts or in Micromedex) | Alternatives: Diet; metformin (<2 x 850 mg/d); insulin; gliclazide may be safer than the other short-acting sulphonilureas. E

preambles.text: The aim of the study was to develop a European list of potentially inappropriate medications (PIM) for older people, which can be used for the analysis and comparison of prescribing patterns across European countries and for clinical practice.

preambles.scope: EU(7)-PIM article: dose and alternative suggestions
preambles.text: The PIM list contains suggestions for dose adjustments and therapeutic alternatives. Dose adjustments and drug alternatives suggested by the experts during the Delphi survey were compiled and included in the EU(7)-PIM list, prioritising in each case those made by the higher number of experts. Suggestions were complemented, if necessary, with information available from the other PIM lists and from Micromedex® [[32](http://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC4464049/#CR32)], a commercially available database which contains comprehensive information on drug use.

footnotes_and_definitions.text: E: Experts; M: Micromedex ® [32]; P: PRISCUS list [22]; L: Laroche et al (2007) [3]; McL: McLeod et al (1997) [26]; B: Beers list (2012) [18].
Note: if nothing is stated under “Dose adjustment / special considerations of use”, this means that no suggestion was made either by the experts or in Micromedex® .

'In lists' gives the numbered prior PIM lists in which the substance appears, with Category A (precisely this active substance is named as a PIM) or Category B (a PIM only in certain clinical conditions or comorbidities, or not named but covered as a PIM drug class). 'Does not appear as PIM' means the substance was not a PIM in those prior lists; it is still an entry of the EU(7)-PIM list and is not an exclusion. Entries the panel judged questionable carry footnote d.
